newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey 1996 budget deficit 1,200 trillion lira.
newsitem.headline: Turkey 1996 budget deficit 1,200 trillion lira.

text.p: Turkey's Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan said on Wednesday the 1996 budget deficit was 1,200 trillion lira compared with an earlier forecast of 1,300 trillion and 316.6 trillion a year earlier.
"It can be seen that the 1996 budget closed with a deficit of 1,200 trillion lira," Erbakan said in a statement at a meeting of economy officials.

The sharp rise in Turkey's budget deficit from a year earlier reflected public sector wage rises, a poorer than expected performance on privatisation and higher basic farm prices, according to analysts.
For 1997 parliament has approved a balanced budget drafted by Islamist premier Erbakan's coalition with conservatives, which took power last June.
Analysts forecast the 1997 budget deficit will be more than 1,500 trillion lira.
Ahead of Wednesday's meeting Erbakan said the improvement on the earlier budget forecast was the result of measures taken and savings made in the last six months of the year.
He said measures during that period had helped lengthen the maturity of government debt paper to 13 months and brought interest rates down to 90 percent.
